overview.body:
**Wiraqucha** ​(*viracocha*) ‌— Creator, ‌Sky, ​Sea ​Foam · ​Sea ​of ​fat — ‌belongs ​to ​the ‌Incan tradition, ​where ‌it ​is catalogued ‌under ​the ​domain ​"Creator, Sky, ​Sea ​Foam". ‌The name ​means ‌"Sea ​of fat".

‌**Wiraqucha** ​is ‌creator, ​sky, sea ‌foam. ​The ​name means ‌"Sea ‌of ‌fat" ​and belongs ​to ‌the ​incan tradition.

​PuniCodex ‌restores ​the name ​as ‌**Wiraqucha** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/viracocha/). ​The ‌restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ​or ​diacritics its ‌ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ‌which ​places ‌the ​name in ​Tier ​2. ‌The plain ​ASCII ​form ​*viracocha* survives ‌as ​a ​modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the ‌early domain-name ​system; ‌the ​restoration, ‌not the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation survives ‌for ​this name; ​**Wiraqucha** is ​a ​scholarly transliteration ​of the ‌reconstructed ​spoken form. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "Sea ‌of fat".

​The ‌ASCII form ​*viracocha* survives ​only ​because the ​early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry diacritics; ‌it ​is a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ​restoration **Wiraqucha** ​recovers the ‌full ‌diacritic detail ‌of the ​scholarly ​transliteration directly ‌in the ​address ​bar. The ‌restoration needs ​no ​distinctive letters ‌or diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form ​would lose, ​which places ​the ​name in ‌Tier 2.

‌The ​letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

- ​**v** ​→ **W** ‌— W
‌- ‌**i** → ‌**i** — ​Same
‌- **r** ​→ **r** ​— ​Same
- ‌**a** → ​**a** ​— Same
​- **c** ‌→ ​**q** — ​Q
- ​**o** ‌→ **u** ​— U: ‌quechua ​qu cluster
‌- **c** ​→ ‌**c** — ‌Same
- ​**h** ​→ **h** ​— Same
​- ‌**a** → ‌**a** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/viracocha/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**viracocha** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Wiraqucha.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"viracocha" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Wiraqucha".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"viracocha" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Wiraqucha" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Wiraqucha was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Wiraqucha ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Wiraqucha ‌place ​creator, sky, ​sea ​foam at ​the ​center of ‌a ​living ​mythological world.

‌### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Wiraqucha ​appears in ‌incan ​tradition ​as creator, ​sky, ​sea foam. ​The ‌name's ​meaning, "Sea ‌of ​fat", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ​and Memory ‌(Cult)

‌Devotees and ‌later ​tradition-keepers ​preserved Wiraqucha ‌in ​ritual, text, ​and ‌iconography, ​ensuring the ​name ‌survived into ​the ‌modern scholarly ​record.

​The ​myths of ​Wiraqucha ‌survive in ‌fragments, ​summaries, ‌and later ​retellings. ​Each version ‌reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ​tellers — ‌poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. The ‌PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ​privilege ‌a single ​version; ​it ​gathers the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers ​can compare ‌them. ​The ‌restoration Wiraqucha ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Wiraqucha ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Wiraqucha, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​creator ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Wiraqucha is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea of ​creator, ​Sky, ‌Sea ​Foam in ​the ‌mind ​and to ‌ask ​what ‌of ​it endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Sea of ‌fat" ​— ‌and ​a name ‌that ​carries ‌its ​meaning so ‌openly ​invites ​meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name ​as creator, ‌Sky, ​Sea ​Foam ‌· Sea ​of ‌fat.

​Sit ​with the ​restored ​form ‌— ‌Wiraqucha — ​and ‌the ​diacritics themselves ​become ‌the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ​a ‌small ​act of ​attention, ​a ‌refusal ​to let ​the ​plain ‌ASCII ​form *viracocha* ​stand ​in ‌for ​the whole. ‌What ​the ‌tradition preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
